passages.text: Be as in love as you can be. Love is existence itself; wherever you flee from it, you flee from yourself.
When words fall silent, the heart begins to speak. Listen to the deep stillness within you; the answer is already there.
Enter through the crack of light in the wound. The broken place is where the light meets you.
You are a guest in this world, yet your heart is searching for a home. Look for it not outside, but within.
Yesterday is gone, tomorrow has not arrived. This moment is the only truth in your hands; hold it lightly, but completely.
The earth carries the seed patiently, and then it becomes a flower. The silence within you will also bloom; do not hurry it.
Do not search for truth far away; it stands behind the eye that is looking, in your breath, in this very line.
Every parting is the beginning of a reunion. What you think you have lost may be the very path that returns you to yourself.
The heart is the throne of the Beloved; the Beloved looks into the heart. Walk gently — do not wound the very thing you carry.
Know what you love, but do not become a burden to it. True love keeps an open hand, not a clenched one.
Whoever looks down from on high ends up alone at the height. Be low like the earth, so that every seed may grow upon you.
This world is a bridge — cross it, but do not build a house on it. Tie your heart to what does not pass away.
Whoever cannot look at all peoples with one eye is, in truth, a rebel, however learned they may seem. Set aside division, and look at the whole.
Nothing is harvested before it ripens, nothing is eaten before it is cooked. The ripeness within you, too, will come in its own time.
Knowledge is to know — and to know is to know yourself. If you do not know yourself, what is the use of all your reading?
The moment you stop searching, what you sought may feel as if it had been beside you all along. Stop. Take a breath.
The Tao that can be named is not the eternal Tao. Stop trying to grasp it; simply be within the flow.
The sage acts without forcing, teaches without speaking. As water wears down stone, softness overcomes hardness.
The highest good is like water; it benefits all things without contending. It flows to the places others avoid, and so it is close to the Tao.
A vessel is useful because of the emptiness within it. Look at the emptiness within yourself the same way; it is the source of fullness.
Set aside ornament, embrace simplicity. Lessen your needs, soften your wants; then your natural state returns.
The bent becomes whole, the crooked becomes straight. The little is gained, the much is bewildering.
Nature speaks little, and that is the lesson: a violent wind does not last all morning, a sudden rain does not last all day.
Knowing others is wisdom; knowing yourself is enlightenment. Mastering others takes strength; mastering yourself takes true power.
All that we are is shaped by the mind. Speak or act with a pure mind, and happiness follows like a shadow that never leaves.
Let go of anger with love, not with anger. You do not put out a spark by throwing another flame on it.
Do not chase after the past, do not worry about the future. Life is found in this moment, in this breath.
Awareness is the path to the deathless; carelessness is the path to death. The watchful never die; the careless are already as if dead.
You build a raft to cross the river, but once across, you do not carry it on your back. Do not mistake the means for the end.
All beings fear suffering, all beings love life. See yourself in others; neither harm, nor cause harm.
Though one may conquer a thousand on the battlefield, the one who conquers themselves wins the greater victory.
A water jar is filled drop by drop. The wise person fills with goodness, gathered little by little.
Distinguish between what is in your power and what is not. Your peace is in direct proportion to how clearly you make this distinction.
When you wake, tell yourself: today I will meet people who are rude, ungrateful, arrogant. But I, too, stand under the same sun as they do.
External things cannot touch your soul; your distress arises from your own judgment about them.
Do not act as though you had ten thousand years to live. While you live, while it is in your power, be good.
You have no time to spend on the past or the future; all you hold is this brief moment. Use it wisely.
What is in keeping with the nature of the universe is also in keeping with your own nature. Move with the current; do not resist it.
The best revenge is to not be like the one who caused the harm. Guard your own character; it is a gift no one else can give or take.
People seek retreats in the country, by the sea, in the mountains. But you can withdraw into yourself any time you wish; nowhere is more peaceful than your own soul.
The master kept pouring tea into a full cup until it overflowed. "You are like this cup," he said. "Until you empty your own opinions, you cannot receive anything new."
A monk said the same words whether he was sad or joyful: "This too is so." He neither mourned nor celebrated; he simply saw.
"Before enlightenment, chop wood, carry water. After enlightenment, chop wood, carry water." The task does not change; how you see it does.
A student asked, "What is Zen?" The master kept drinking his tea without answering. Some questions are answered by silence.
The finger points at the moon, but the finger is not the moon. Words point toward truth, but words are not truth itself.
The wind blows, the leaf falls; neither the wind nor the leaf is at fault. Things happen — watch, before you name them.
The stone does not try to stop the water, nor the water to wear down the stone. Yet over the years, water wins — patiently, without effort.
A monk was asked, "Which is the most sacred day?" "Today," he said, "because it is the only day we have."
Is it not a joy to learn and, from time to time, to put what is learned into practice? Knowledge ripens not in a single moment, but through return.
The person of virtue acts first, and speaks afterward according to their actions. Consistency speaks louder than words.
To know what you know, and to know what you do not know — this is true knowledge.
To make a mistake and not correct it — this is the real mistake. It is not the falling, but choosing to remain on the ground, that diminishes a person.
Finding the middle way is the most difficult virtue, for it takes courage to avoid both extremes.
Do not do to others what you would not want done to yourself. This simple sentence is the essence of all ethics.
Only when the cold of winter comes do we know that the pine and cypress are the last to lose their leaves. Hardship reveals what is rooted.
The noble person is calm and spacious; the small person is forever anxious. Spaciousness comes from within, not from without.

title: Inspired by The School of Gods
author: Stefano E. D'Anna

passages.text: Thought is destiny. A thought that circles again and again in your mind is the first step of the road you will walk tomorrow — decide where you want it to lead.
Fear is love that has decayed. If you are afraid of losing something, it is because you still love it deeply; look beneath the fear, and love is waiting there.
The past is dust, but the moment in your hands is always fresh. Shake the dust off it; today's light is already falling on you.
To love your enemy does not mean to surrender to them. Listen even to your harshest inner critic as a teacher; it too is trying to show you something.
The world is a tale, but you choose which tale you tell. The same scene can be seen as a prison or as a school.
To do only what you love does not mean to do what is easy. Follow what your heart says yes to; everything else falls into place on its own.
"I am you" is not a comfort, it is a reminder. What you see when you look at another is, in some way, also a part of you.
Believe first, then see. More often than not, the proof you are waiting for arrives only after you make room for it.

title: Words of Kadın Ana, the Mother
author: Anatolian Oral Tradition

passages.text: Kadın Ana was the first hand to sow a seed into the earth. You, too, cannot know in which season the small seed you plant today will bear fruit — plant it anyway.
In Kadın Ana's community, what was produced was for sharing, not hoarding. When you share what you have without keeping score, you repeat the oldest wisdom there is.
Like the Alevi sister-dervishes who endured in silence through dark ages, sometimes the only form wisdom takes is patience — carrying your truth quietly within.
In the order Kadın Ana shaped, there was no ruler and no servant — only a burden carried together. Look for someone to help carry what you are carrying today.
They say the wind still carries Kadın Ana's voice from one mountain to another. Some wisdom is not kept in books, but in a whisper carried by the wind.
Knowledge finds its true worth only when it is handed to someone ready to carry it. Whatever you have gathered, prepare to one day pass it on.
Ancient knowledge is abandoned, a little more each day, for small and fleeting gains. Even pausing today to remember an old saying is a small act of preservation.
The Mother of the Luvians was later reborn under other names, as other goddesses. A thing may change its shape, but its root stays in the same earth.
